chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Hamadani from Ibn 'Atiyyah from Ismail ibn Jabir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who combs his beard seventy times, counting each stroke individually, Satan will not approach him for forty mornings.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for combing one's beard seventy times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this specific practice of combing the beard seventy times with deliberate counting as a means of spiritual purification and protection from Satan for forty days. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *Zinat* (adornment) as an act of worship, where physical grooming serves as a tangible discipline to maintain spiritual vigilance and repel negative influences.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by al-Hussain b. Ahmad from Sahl b. Ziyad from Ibrahim b. Abdulrahman b. al-Hajjaj from Muhammad b. Umar al-Hamadani from Ibn ’Atiyyah from Ismail b. Jabir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said who said: “
Shaitaan will remain aloof for next forty days from one who combs his beard seventy times.”
